name: libaco
workload: Pure context switch cost, acosw versus libco's coctx_swap, 20 million resume calls (40 million switches) on x86_64.
claimed_speedup: acosw is 1.72x faster than Tencent libco's coctx_swap (17.64 ns/op in the benchmark branch); README states about 10 ns per coroutine switch with a standalone stack.
compiler_and_flags: -DACO_CONFIG_SHARE_FPU_MXCSR_ENV, tcmalloc_minimal; README example builds with gcc -g -O2
hardware: AWS c5d.large virtual machine, RHEL-7.5, 2018-06-30 (exact CPU model not stated)
tradeoffs: Asymmetric coroutines only, x86_64 and i386 Sys V ABI plus limited others; C API; no scheduler; shared-stack mode copies stack contents, which slows switches as copied size grows.
caveats: Numbers from 2018 on a cloud VM with no CPU model; benchmark compares only the switch routine against libco, not Boost.Context. Last commit is a README typo fix (2022). Verified from the benchmark branch page via WebFetch; the author's own benchmark, so first-party. The libaco HN thread was surfaced by search but not opened.
found_via: Blogs / talks (personal and company engineering blogs, conference talks): WebSearch 'libaco asymmetric coroutine C benchmark context switch vs libco Boost.Context ucontext'

name: libcopp
workload: Coroutine switch overhead in ns with 1, 1,000 and 30,000 live coroutines (64 KB stacks for the high-count tests).
claimed_speedup: Switch overhead: libcopp 77 / 105 / 273 ns versus libco static stack pool 84 / 168 / 450 ns (1 / 1,000 / 30,000 coroutines); versus libco 4K shared stack 83 / 529 / 1,073 ns. Gap is about 1.1x at 1 coroutine and about 1.65x at 30,000 (ratios derived from page data).
compiler_and_flags: -O2 (per gist summary); compiler version not confirmed
tradeoffs: Stackful and C++20 stackless modes, stack pools, optional Intel TSX; uses Boost.Context-style assembly switching on supported platforms. Heavier API than a bare switch library.
caveats: Numbers are from a 2019 gist by the maintainer; hardware not stated; the benchmark does not include Boost.Context or Boost.Coroutine rows, only libco, libgo (2018 build), C++20 coroutines, goroutines and ucontext. The repo's README says latest benchmarks are in GitHub Actions CI, which was not opened.
